For complete endpoint references, visit the [Official HighLevel API Documentation](marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/) .

...

## **HighLevel API Documentation**

The official API documentation provides information about available endpoints, authentication, request parameters, response formats, and supported API versions. Developers can use this documentation to:

* Explore available API endpoints.
* Review authentication requirements.
* Check supported API versions.
* Build and maintain custom integrations.
* Understand endpoint-specific restrictions.

**Note:** New legacy API key generation is being phased out. Private Integration Tokens and OAuth 2.0 are the recommended authentication methods.

...

## **How to Use Versioned API Documentation**

Versioned API documentation allows developers to reference the correct API version when building or maintaining integrations.

1. Open the [HighLevel API Documentation](marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/) .
2. Select the required API version using the version switcher.
3. Review the available endpoints, parameters, and response formats.
4. Use the appropriate version when developing or updating integrations.

API V3 is available for supported endpoints. Availability varies by endpoint.

[Screenshot: API documentation version switcher]

* * *

## **API Access Across HighLevel Plans**

HighLevel offers API access across its subscription plans, including Starter, Unlimited, and Founder.

Both OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens (PIT) are available across plans. However, access to specific API endpoints depends on subscription eligibility, permissions, and scopes.

**API Availability by Plan  
**

|API Capability |Starter ($97/month) |Unlimited ($297/month) |Founder ($497/month) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|OAuth 2.0 |Available |Available |Available |
|Private Integration Tokens |Available |Available |Available |
|Standard API Endpoints |Available\* |Available |Available |
|Higher-Tier Restricted Endpoints |Restricted |Restricted |Subject to endpoint eligibility |

\*Standard endpoint access is subject to applicable permissions and endpoint-specific restrictions.

...

**Plan-Restricted API Endpoints**

While standard API access is available across plans, certain operations require higher-tier subscriptions. The following endpoints are currently documented as requiring Founders plan access:

|Endpoint |Purpose |
| --- | --- |
|Create Sub-Account |Create sub-accounts programmatically. |
|Enable SaaS for Sub-Account |Enable SaaS functionality for a sub-account. |

Refer to the [Official API Reference](marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/) for endpoint-specific requirements.

...

## **API Authentication Methods**

HighLevel supports two primary authentication methods for modern API integrations.

**Private Integration Tokens (PIT)**

Private Integration Tokens allow developers to securely connect internal applications to HighLevel. They are suitable for account-specific integrations and allow permissions to be managed through assigned scopes.

**OAuth 2.0**

OAuth 2.0 allows applications to request authorized access to HighLevel accounts. It is commonly used for public integrations, Marketplace applications, and applications requiring user authorization.

**Note:** The availability of an authentication method does not guarantee access to every API endpoint.

For setup instructions, see [Private Integrations: Everything You Need to Know](help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003054-private-integrations-everything-you-need-to-know) .

...

### **How to Request a New API Endpoint**

If an endpoint is not available in the official API documentation, developers can submit a feature request through the [HighLevel API Documentation GitHub repository](github.com/GoHighLevel/highlevel-api-docs/issues) .

Review the existing documentation before submitting a request.

* * *

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Is API access available on all HighLevel plans?**

Yes. HighLevel provides API access across Starter ($97/month), Unlimited ($297/month), and Founder ($497/month) plans. OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens (PIT) are available across all plans. However, access to specific API endpoints depends on subscription eligibility, required scopes, and permissions. The Founder Plan, formerly Agency Pro, includes higher-tier API capabilities and access to eligible restricted endpoints.

For current subscription details, refer to [HighLevel Pricing](gohighlevel.com/pricing) .

...

**Q: Is API V1 still supported?**

No. API V1 reached end-of-support on December 31, 2025. Existing integrations may continue functioning, but updates and technical support are no longer provided.

**Q: What authentication methods are supported?**

HighLevel supports Private Integration Tokens and OAuth 2.0 for modern API integrations.

**Q: Is API V3 available?**

Yes. API V3 is available for supported endpoints. Developers should review the API documentation for version-specific availability.

# How to Setup and Use the HighLevel MCP Server

Modified on: Sun, 15 Nov, 2026 at 2:10 AM

Connect your AI assistant to HighLevel so it can find CRM records and perform supported actions from your instructions. The HighLevel MCP Server, also called the LeadConnector MCP Server, connects through OAuth: sign in, choose the sub-account or sub-accounts to include, and approve the requested permissions.

This guide covers setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, Muse, and Grok Bot, along with how to work across authorized sub-accounts and discover available operations.

...

# **What is the HighLevel MCP Server?**

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It gives AI assistants a standard way to discover and use tools from connected applications. With the HighLevel MCP Server, your assistant can work with supported CRM data and actions without you needing to know the underlying API.

The active catalog includes **more than 600 read, create, update, and delete operations across 38 domains** . The operations available to your connection depend on the OAuth scopes and permissions you approve.

* * *

## **Before You Connect**

You need access to the HighLevel sub-account or sub-accounts you want to connect and a supported AI client. ChatGPT users can find the official HighLevel plugin in Plugins. Muse and Grok Bot also offer officially listed apps. For custom MCP connections, use the corresponding URL below.

|AI client |Connection method |
| --- | --- |

...

## **Permissions and Security**

* **You select the sub-accounts.** Each request is authorized against the installation and can access only a sub-account included in that connection.
* **OAuth scopes limit actions.** The assistant can perform only the operations allowed by your grant.
* **Sensitive actions have additional checks.** Sensitive and irreversible operations are subject to confirmation and safety checks before execution.
* **You control ongoing access.** Review or revoke the connection's access from your LeadConnector account.

* * *

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

#### **Q: Do I need a Private Integration Token?**

The client connections in this guide use OAuth. Complete the LeadConnector sign-in and consent flow to authorize access; you do not need to manually create or rotate a token for these connections.

excerpts:
Version: v3

On this page

# HighLevel MCP Server

**Stop clicking. Start asking.**

Your next booking, follow-up, or invoice can start with a sentence. Connect HighLevel to your AI assistant, then ask it to find a contact, book an appointment, send a message, update a deal, or schedule a social post. The assistant works directly with your HighLevel account, so you can get work done from the conversation you’re already having.

...

## Stay in control ​

The assistant only gets the access you give it, and HighLevel checks that access every time it acts.

* **You choose the sub-accounts.** The assistant can only work in the sub-accounts you selected when you connected.
* **You choose the permissions.** It can only take actions your approved permissions allow, and each action is checked again when it runs.
* **No passwords or API keys to share.** You sign in on HighLevel’s own sign-in page. Your assistant never sees your password.

...

### Do I need an API key or a Private Integration token? ​

No. You connect by signing in with your HighLevel login, choosing your sub-account(s), and approving the requested permissions. There’s no key to create, paste, or rotate.

...

### Is this the same as the Developer MCP Server? ​

No. This server connects AI assistants to the data in your HighLevel sub-accounts. The [Marketplace Developer MCP Server](marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/sdk/marketplace-cli/mcp) is a separate tool that helps developers build and release Marketplace apps.

# OAuth 2.0

Copy page Copied!

Open in

OAuth 2.0 is a standard protocol that authorizes a client application (like a third-party app) to access specific resources on behalf of a user, without sharing the user’s password. It’s widely used for APIs that need secure, delegated access.

HighLevel supports the **Authorization Code Grant** flow with v2 APIs. Below is the step-by-step procedure to understand and use the OAuth 2.0 flow.

* * *

## 1\. Register an OAuth App ​

1. Go to the [Marketplace](marketplace.gohighlevel.com/) and sign up for a developer account.
2. Go to My Apps, click Create App.
3. Fill in the following details:

...

+ **Who can install** : Who should be able to view and install the app from the Marketplace UI?
         The recommended setting is `“Both Agency & Sub-account”` to ensure maximum visibility and adoption of your app.
         However, if you’re building a fully white-labeled SaaS feature intended to be exclusively discovered and installed by agencies for use within their sub-accounts, you may choose to limit visibility to Agencies only.
    + **Listing Type:** White-label recommended for marketing agencies.

drawing

  
1. After creating the APP you will be taken to the Profile section where you will need to add the details related to your APP. For eg; APP Logo, category, Company Name, APP Description, preview images etc.
2. After completing the profile details, please click on the Advanced Settings drop down available in the left pane and go to the auth section.
3. The Auth page will appear as shown in the screenshot below. This is where you’ll configure essential settings for your app’s OAuth integration, including scopes, redirect URLs, and client credentials.

drawing

  
* **Scopes:** Scopes define the level of access your app will have — what data it can read or what actions it can perform on behalf of the user. [Click Here](marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/Authorization/Scopes) to find all the available Scopes.
  
    + It’s best practice to request the minimum number of scopes necessary for your app to function.
    + Click on the "Select Scope" dropdown and choose the relevant scopes based on your app’s functionality.
* **Redirect URL:** A Redirect URL (also known as a Callback URL) is the destination where the authorization server will send the authorization code after the user installs the app.

...

+ Enter your redirect URL in the Redirect URL field.
    + Click the "Add" button to save it.
* **Client Keys (ID & Secret):** In the Client Keys section:
  
    + Click the "Add" button.
    + Provide a name for your client key pair.
    + Upon saving, your Client ID and Client Secret will be generated.

These credentials are used to identify and authenticate your application with the OAuth server during token exchange.

**Important:** Be sure to copy and securely store your Client Secret immediately. After clicking "OK", you will not be able to view or copy the secret again from the UI.

* * *

## 2\. Add the App to Your Desired Location ​

* Have the location/agency admin visit your Installation URL.
* Select the location to connect.
* Redirected to your Redirect URL with an Authorization Code.
* Exchange the code for an Access Token via the OAuth 2.0 [Get Access Token](marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/oauth/get-access-token) API.
* Use the Access Token to call APIs.

...

## 3\. Get the Installation URL ​

Inside your APP Auth Pane available inside the Advanced Settings Section you will be able to see the Install Link at the top of the Page.

drawing

  
Click on the Show button and you will be able to see the Installation URLs which you will be using to install the APP.

drawing

  
Depending on your usecase and account setup you can either use the standard or the whitelabel version of the Installation URL.

Refer to the below steps to install the APP:

1. Copy the Installation URL and open it in your browser.
2. In case you are not logged in to your GHL account it will ask you to login to your account.

drawing

  
* In case you are logged in it will show a page showcasing the accounts.

drawing

  
1. Select the account you want to install the APP in.
2. When a user grants access, their browser is redirected to the specified redirect URI, and the Authorization Code is passed inside the code query parameter.

```
https : //myapp.com/oauth/callback/highlevel?code=7676cjcbdc6t76cdcbkjcd09821jknnkj
```

...

Sample Payload:

```
curl -X POST "services.leadconnectorhq.com/oauth/token" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "client_id": "665c6bb13d4e5364bdec0e2f-mawqjyjd", "client_secret": "74032272-7f45-4e07-8717-5e1ddbfe3de0", "grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": "363fe3f086e2db02bb9c34722902d21f76c9b217", "user_type": "Company", "redirect_uri": "myapp.com/oauth/callback/highlevel" }'
```

...

## 8\. Create Sub-Account Token from Agency Token ​

Suppose you have an Agency-level Access Token but want to run API endpoints specific to a Sub-Account (Location). In that case, you can use the Agency-level Access Token to generate a Sub-Account/Location-level Access Token via the [Get Location Access Token from Agency Token](marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/oauth/get-location-access-token) API endpoint.

excerpts:
Requirements

* Node.js >= 18.0.0
* TypeScript >= 4.0 (if using TypeScript)

Authentication

The HighLevel API supports three types of authentication tokens with different levels of access:

1. Private Integration Token

* Highest priority - Used for private integrations
* Full access to all API endpoints
* Managed through your HighLevel app settings

2. Agency Access Token

* Used for agency-level operations
* Access to agency and sub-account data
* Obtained through OAuth 2.0 flow

3. Location Access Token

* Used for location-specific operations
* Access to single location data
* Obtained through OAuth 2.0 flow

Getting Started

Basic Setup

TypeScript

import HighLevel, { MongoDBSessionStorage, LogLevel } from '@gohighlevel/api-client';
// or
import { HighLevel } from '@gohighlevel/api-client';

// Initialize with private integration token
const ghl = new HighLevel({
  privateIntegrationToken: 'your-private-integration-token',
  logLevel: LogLevel.INFO
});

GoHighLevel API: Docs, Auth, Limits and Examples
excerpts:
* Use a Private Integration token for your own account and OAuth 2.0 for an app other accounts will install. Legacy API keys only work on v1, which reached end of support on December 31, 2025.
* Every request needs Authorization: Bearer <token> and a Version header.
* Limits are 100 requests per 10 seconds and 200,000 a day, per app per sub-account.
* Many “API” jobs are simpler as a webhook inside a GoHighLevel workflow.
* HighLevel now has official Node, Python and PHP SDKs and an MCP server for AI assistants.

Where is the GoHighLevel API documentation?

The main reference is HighLevel’s developer portal. Each endpoint page lists its URL, scopes, the token type it accepts and example requests. Checked November 16, 2026:
* API reference: marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs , with every endpoint grouped by area.

...

* OAuth 2.0 | An app that other HighLevel accounts install from the Marketplace | Authorization code flow. Access tokens last a day; refresh tokens last a year unless used
* Legacy API key | Nothing new | Works only on v1, which is past end of support. New key generation is being phased out
Private Integration tokens work at both the agency and the sub-account level. A sub-account token can only touch that sub-account’s data; an agency token reaches agency endpoints. Some endpoints are marked “OAuth access token only” and reject Private Integration tokens, so check the endpoint page before you build around one (checked Nov 16, 2026 on marketplace.gohighlevel.com ) .

How to create a Private Integration token

1. Open the right level. For one business, open its sub-account. For agency-wide work, use the agency view.
2. Go to Settings → Private Integrations. If you don’t see it, check that the feature is turned on in Labs.

Refer to the documentation (marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/oauth/get-access-token) for more details on how to obtain the access token.
To create a GET endpoint for OAuth in your application:
* Choose a route for your endpoint (e.g., "/OAuth/callback/gohighlevel").
* Configure your application to listen for requests to this route.
* When a user authorizes your application, GoHighLevel will redirect them to your endpoint with a "code" parameter.
* Retrieve the "code" parameter from the request.
* Store the code securely.
* Make a POST request to GoHighLevel's "/OAuth/token" endpoint with the code, client ID, client secret, grant type, and redirect URI.
* Capture the response from the POST request.
* Extract the access token, token type, expiration time, refresh token, and other relevant information from the response.

README.md

GoHighLevel MCP Server

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server providing access to the complete GoHighLevel API. This server enables AI assistants like Claude to interact with GoHighLevel's services including contacts, opportunities, calendars, workflows, and more.
GoHighLevel Server MCP server

🚀 Quick Start

npx @drausal/gohighlevel-mcp
Or install globally:
npm install -g @drausal/gohighlevel-mcp

🚀 Features

* Complete API Coverage : Access to all GoHighLevel API endpoints
* OAuth2 Support : Automatic token management and refresh
* Bearer Token Auth : Simple API key authentication
* Type-Safe : Full TypeScript implementation with Zod validation
* Stdio Transport : Works with Claude Desktop and other MCP clients
* Auto-Generated : Built from the official OpenAPI specification

📋 Prerequisites

* Node.js >= 20.0.0
* A GoHighLevel account with API access
* API credentials (Bearer token or OAuth2 client credentials)

🔧 Installation

Quick Start with npx (Recommended)

No installation needed! Use npx to run the server directly:
npx @drausal/gohighlevel-mcp

Alternative: Install Globally

For permanent installation:
npm install -g @drausal/gohighlevel-mcp
Then run:
gohighlevel-mcp

From Source (Development)

...

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gohighlevel": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "/absolute/path/to/gohighlevel-mcp/build/index.js"
      ],
      "env": {
        "BEARER_TOKEN_BEARERAUTH": "your_api_key_here",
        "BEARER_TOKEN_BEARER": "your_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}

Warp Terminal Configuration

For Warp users, use the npx method:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gohighlevel": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "@drausal/gohighlevel-mcp"
      ],
      "env": {
        "BEARER_TOKEN_BEARERAUTH": "your_api_key_here",
        "BEARER_TOKEN_BEARER": "your_api_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}

Running Standalone

# With npx
npx @drausal/gohighlevel-mcp

# With global installation
gohighlevel-mcp

# From source
pnpm start

🔐 Authentication

Bearer Token

The simplest authentication method. Get your API key from GoHighLevel:
1. Log into your GoHighLevel account
2. Go to Settings → API
3. Copy your API key
4. Set BEARER_TOKEN_BEARERAUTH in your .env file

OAuth2

For more advanced use cases with automatic token refresh:
1. Agency Access : For agency-level operations
* Set OAUTH_CLIENT_ID_AGENCY_ACCESS and OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET_AGENCY_ACCESS
2. Location Access : For location-specific operations
* Set OAUTH_CLIENT_ID_LOCATION_ACCESS and OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET_LOCATION_ACCESS
The server automatically:
* Obtains access tokens using client credentials flow
* Caches tokens for their lifetime
* Refreshes tokens when expired
See docs/oauth2-configuration.md for detailed OAuth2 configuration.

📚 Available Tools

The MCP server exposes all GoHighLevel API endpoints as MCP tools. Major categories include:

Core Resources

* Contacts : Create, update, search contacts
* Opportunities : Manage sales pipeline
* Calendars : Schedule appointments
* Workflows : Trigger and manage automation

Communication

* Conversations : Messaging and chat
* Emails : Email campaigns and templates
* SMS : Text message campaigns

## 6. Refresh Token Usage

As shown in the previous response, the Access Token expires after 86,399 seconds, which is approximately 24 hours. This means you'll need to regenerate a new Access Token once it expires to continue making API requests.

However, regenerating an Access Token using the authorization code requires repeating the entire installation process, which can be time-consuming. To simplify this, we also provide a Refresh Token along with the Access Token.

The Refresh Token is valid for up to one year, or until it is used. Once you use a Refresh Token to obtain a new Access Token, the original Refresh Token becomes invalid, and the response will include a new Refresh Token along with the new Access Token.
If left unused, the Refresh Token will remain valid for one year.

To generate a new Access Token using your existing Refresh Token, use the following API endpoint: Get Access Token

* Access Tokens expire after ~24 hours.
* Refresh Tokens are valid for 1 year or until used.
* Use Refresh Token to obtain a new Access Token without reinstallation.

# GoHighLevel API: a practical guide to the docs, authentication and limits

The GoHighLevel API is HighLevel’s REST API for reading and changing data in a HighLevel account: contacts, opportunities, calendars, conversations, payments, workflows and more. Requests go to

```
https://services.leadconnectorhq.com
```

, the documentation lives on HighLevel’s developer portal at marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs, and every request needs a bearer token and a

```
Version
```

header.

The official docs list every endpoint. What they don’t tell you is which token to use, which version to send, where the limits bite, or when you shouldn’t be using the API at all. This guide covers that practical layer, with examples from integrations we’ve built for clients.

Key takeaways

* Use a Private Integration token for your own account and OAuth 2.0 for an app other accounts will install. Legacy API keys only work on v1, which reached end of support on December 31, 2025.
* Every request needs

  ```
  Authorization: Bearer <token>
  ```

  and a

  ```
  Version
  ```

  header.
* Limits are 100 requests per 10 seconds and 200,000 a day, per app per sub-account.
* Many “API” jobs are simpler as a webhook inside a GoHighLevel workflow.
* HighLevel now has official Node, Python and PHP SDKs and an MCP server for AI assistants.

## Where is the GoHighLevel API documentation?

The main reference is HighLevel’s developer portal. Each endpoint page lists its URL, scopes, the token type it accepts and example requests. Checked November 16, 2026:

* API reference: marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs, with every endpoint grouped by area.
* Getting started: HighLevel’s help article on the HighLevel API, which covers plans, versions and the v1 end of support.
* Private Integrations: Private Integrations: everything you need to know.
* AI-readable docs: a plain-text index at marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/llms.txt, useful if you’re building with an AI coding assistant.
* Code: HighLevel’s GitHub has the public API docs, the SDKs and example apps.

## Which GoHighLevel API version should you use?

Use API v2, the modern API, and send the

```
Version
```

header that the endpoint’s docs page shows. The old v1 API is finished: it reached end of support on December 31, 2025, and while existing v1 integrations may keep running, nothing new should be built on it (checked on help.gohighlevel.com).

| Version | Status (November 2026) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v1 (API keys) | End of support since December 31, 2025 | Rebuild any integration still on it |
| 2021-04-15, 2021-07-28, 2023-02-21 | Supported | Same endpoints and schemas; only the Version header value differs. Most published examples use 2021-07-28 |
| v3 | Latest, released June 11, 2026 | Named versions from here on (v3, v4). Adds newer endpoints, including the limited workflow builder API |

## How do you authenticate with the GoHighLevel API?

There are two current ways to authenticate, and the choice depends on whose account the integration runs in.

| Method | Use it for | How it works |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Private Integration token | Your own sub-account or agency: internal tools, scripts, one client's integration | A fixed token with the scopes you choose, created in Settings. Sent as a bearer token |
| OAuth 2.0 | An app that other HighLevel accounts install from the Marketplace | Authorization code flow. Access tokens last a day; refresh tokens last a year unless used |
| Legacy API key | Nothing new | Works only on v1, which is past end of support. New key generation is being phased out |

Private Integration tokens work at both the agency and the sub-account level. A sub-account token can only touch that sub-account’s data; an agency token reaches agency endpoints. Some endpoints are marked “OAuth access token only” and reject Private Integration tokens, so check the endpoint page before you build around one (checked on marketplace.gohighlevel.com).

# HighLevel MCP Server

Stop clicking. Start asking.

Your next booking, follow-up, or invoice can start with a sentence. Connect HighLevel to your AI assistant, then ask it to find a contact, book an appointment, send a message, update a deal, or schedule a social post. The assistant works directly with your HighLevel account, so you can get work done from the conversation you’re already having.

More than 700 actions across 38 HighLevel features give you room to hand off everyday work:

* Follow up while the context is fresh. Look up a lead’s messages, check their appointments, and send your
...
-account first.

## Set up your assistant

Every assistant uses the same secure sign-in: sign in with your HighLevel login, choose your sub-account(s), and approve.

### ChatGPT and Codex

HighLevel is an official app in ChatGPT. Custom ChatGPT plugins, Codex, and other compatible OpenAI clients connect to

```
https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/
```

. This address ends with a slash.

#### ChatGPT

1. Open HighLevel in ChatGPT Plugins and connect it.
2. Complete the sign-in (sign in → pick sub-account(s) → approve).
3. Start a new conversation, type

   ```
   @
   ```

   , and select HighLevel.

Or add HighLevel as a custom plugin:

1. Check that your account or workspace allows custom MCP connections.
2. Open ChatGPT Plugins, select the plus button, then Add custom MCP server.
3. Enter a name and description. Under Connection, add

   ```
   https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/
   ```

   as the MCP server URL and complete the connection prompts.
4. Finish creating the plugin and complete the HighLevel sign-in (sign in → pick sub-account(s) → approve).
5. Start a new conversation, type

   ```
   @
   ```

   , and select HighLevel.

For current menu names and availability, see OpenAI’s custom MCP setup guide.

> ▶️ Custom plugin setup video: Connect ChatGPT to HighLevel — watch on Loom

#### Codex

Add the HighLevel server, then start the sign-in:

```
```
codex mcp add highlevel --url https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/  
codex mcp login highlevel
```
```

In the Codex IDE extension, open the gear menu → MCP servers → Add server, choose Streamable HTTP, and enter the same URL. Save the server, select Restart extension, then Authenticate when sign-in is required. See the MCP setup guide.

Other compatible OpenAI clients can use the same address as a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server and complete the sign-in when prompted.

### Claude

Claude connects to

```
https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2
```

.

#### Claude.ai

* Open Claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
* Set the server URL to

  ```
  https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2
  ```

  .
* Click Connect and complete the sign-in (sign in → pick sub-account(s) → approve).
* Start a new chat. The HighLevel tools are now available.

> ▶️ Walkthrough video: Watch on Loom

#### Claude Cowork

* In Claude Cowork, open the connectors / integrations settings and choose Add custom connector.
* Set the server URL to

  ```
  https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2
  ```

  .
* Complete the sign-in (sign in → pick sub-account(s) → approve).
* Your Cowork agents can now use the HighLevel tools.

#### Claude Code (CLI)

```
```
claude mcp add --transport http highlevel https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2
```
```

Or add it to

```
.mcp.json
```

at your project root:

```
```
{  
  "mcpServers": {  
    "highlevel": {  
      "type": "http",  
      "url": "https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2"  
    }  
  }  
}
```
```

Run

```
/mcp
```

in Claude Code and follow the authentication prompts to sign in. Verify the server configuration with

```
claude mcp list
```

. See Claude Code’s MCP guide.
